items.title: Glenn Zottola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 7, 2020

ctx.x: And Bud told me when Louis first came to Chicago, me and Bix Beiderbecke used to go down and to hear this new guy in town. And when we first went there we couldn’t deal with it. We couldn’t understand what the hell he was doing with the time. We never heard anyone lay back like that. Because you know jazz of the 20s was very on top of the beat. So when Louis came in with the New Orleans, King Oliver type time, they couldn’t understand it. He said we went back several times and we finally got to love it. So you…

If someone could, maybe people have done this, sometimes you see a printout of sound waves. You know, the drum, you hit the snare drum and it goes like this. It’s almost like a cardiac chart. And I’m wondering where Louis Armstrong placed his quarter notes in relationship to the beat.
